request.idea: An evil wizard means to summon a demon tonight, certain that he can bind it and use it. He may well complete the ritual, but the binding fails and the demon cannot be controlled: the climax must turn on the wizard’s hubris. The adventure should be creepy, with a dread that grows from what the heroes find and understand, not from blood and gore. Give the heroes real ways to stop or banish the demon: anchors to break, a true name, a counter-rite and a sacrifice, and let what they manage to do along the way weaken the demon or the ritual at the end. An exciting plot with a ticking clock, clues that interlock, side characters with their own wants and secrets, and choices that matter.

seeds.text: The birds are silent. They just sit and watch.
The helpful guide works for the villain, but wants to switch sides.
The heroes have only one night.
To finish their master’s unfinished work.
A sealed letter that was never delivered; the addressee is still alive.
Is convinced they are already dead.

concept.title: The Name in the Bell
concept.tagline: In Ironmere the birds sit silent on every roof, the village murmurs a strange name in its sleep, and at midnight the valley’s healer opens a door he cannot close.
concept.teaser: The letter came without a sender, written in a young and careful hand: the birds of Ironmere have fallen silent, and the bell on Greytor no longer rings. When you reach the valley at sunset, crows, rooks and jackdaws sit on every roof ridge and every fence post, thousands of them, without a sound. Every one of them has its beak turned towards the tower up on the hill.
concept.premise: The wizard Erland Highfield, Ironmere’s beloved healer, means to summon the demon Ukhraalesh at midnight in the crypt beneath the chapel ruin on Greytor and put it in irons. With that he will finish the work that cost his master Herluf his life forty years ago, and he is certain that the name in his iron collar will make the demon his servant. The heroes have one night to understand what he is doing, break the three anchors that hold the door open and find the whole name before the binding fails.
concept.truth: Forty years ago Master Herluf meant to bind the demon Ukhraalesh in the crypt, and he had its whole name cast into a new chapel bell. At the door he understood that no name can bind it, only drive it back; he pulled the serving girl Yrsa out of the circle, where she lay as the gift, gave her a hastily written letter for his apprentice Erland and closed the door from inside with his own life. Erland saw only a master who failed for a serving girl’s sake; he drove Yrsa away, and the letter was never delivered. The little familiar that Herluf himself had called up years before stayed behind when the door closed, and it has sat on Erland’s shoulder ever since, convincing him that the bell’s name was a forgery and that the name it whispered itself, Ukhraal, is the right one. It is only half the name. The bell, which Yrsa has rung every midnight since, kept the demon out until Erland stole its clapper seven nights ago.
concept.conflict: Erland’s hubris against a dead man’s warning: a scholar who would put a demon in irons with half a name, against an old woman, a mute bell and a letter that never arrived.
concept.goal: Keep Ukhraalesh from breaking loose from the crypt on Greytor: break the anchors, drive the demon back or strike it down when Erland’s binding fails at midnight, and save the apprentice Dyre if it can be done.

objective.target: Ukhraalesh, the demon behind the door in the crypt
objective.state: Behind the door in the circle of iron and salt in the crypt beneath the chapel ruin. At midnight the door opens and the demon steps through; Erland’s collar breaks, because the name engraved in it is only half the demon’s name. How strong the demon is depends on the three anchors (see the Door and the Three Anchors in the crypt), and if Dyre lies in the circle, it rides on his heartbeat.
objective.resolution: By force: Ukhraalesh uses the Vrock stat block (AC 15, HP 152) and is weakened by every broken anchor. If it drops to 0 HP, its body dissolves into black feathers and stinking slime, and the door closes; the price is a fight that may cost lives. Without a fight: the counter-rite from Herluf’s letter. The clapper must be hung back in the bell (10 minutes in the bell tower), so that the rope hanging down into the crypt can ring it. Each round while the bell rings, a creature in the circle speaks the whole name and makes a DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) or DC 15 Intelligence (Religion) check; three successes before three failures drive the demon back through the door, which closes. Each failure costs the speaker 10 (3d6) Psychic damage as the demon screams the name back. Or a willing creature walks in through the door with the whole name on its lips: the door closes behind it at once, and it never comes back. If the heroes can do none of these, the demon breaks up through the bell shaft at the end of round 10 and flies towards Ironmere.

concept.stakes: If the heroes fail, Ukhraalesh breaks loose at midnight. First it takes the sleepers who wear Erland’s amulets; in the morning the birds are gone from Ironmere, and so is every soul who slept with an amulet around their neck. Erland becomes its first prey, and the valley its hunting ground.

clock.start: Sunset. The birds have sat silent on Ironmere’s roofs for seven days, and the bell on Greytor has not rung for seven nights. The apprentice Dyre goes from door to door with a basket of Erland’s lead amulets, the last he is to hand out, and Erland waits in his tower.

ticks.event: The village sleeps, and everyone who wears one of Erland’s lead amulets murmurs the half name, Ukhraal, in their sleep. It is the call, and it pulls the door open.
ticks.sign: The same muffled murmur seeps through the shutters from house after house, and the birds on the roofs turn their heads towards the sound. Burn a sleeper’s amulet, and that sleeper alone stops murmuring and wakes.

ticks.event: If Dyre still wears his iron amulet, he falls into a trance and walks up to the crypt to lie down in the circle as the gift. Erland goes down into the crypt to make ready.
ticks.sign: Dyre stops in the middle of a sentence, his eyes roll up, and he walks calmly away, deaf to every word. Every flame on Greytor burns blue and gives no warmth. Tear the iron amulet off him, and he collapses and wakes.

ticks.event: If the call still stands, the sleepers rise and walk in their nightclothes up the road to Greytor, where they stand silent around the chapel ruin like a congregation.
ticks.sign: A long line of people without lanterns on the road up, eyes open and mouths murmuring; the doors of Ironmere stand open behind them. Each burnt amulet wakes its wearer.

ticks.event: The door in the crypt opens, and Ukhraalesh steps through. Erland speaks the half name and closes the collar around its neck, and the collar breaks.
ticks.sign: Every bird in the valley takes off at once, a thunder of wings in the dark, and then everything goes still. From now on the heroes have 10 rounds before the demon breaks out.

clock.costs: The road between Ironmere and Greytor: 30 minutes. Searching an area: 10 minutes. Hanging the clapper back in the bell: 10 minutes. Burning Ironmere’s amulets: 1 hour with the elder’s help, 2 hours in secret, house by house. A short rest: 1 hour.
clock.deadline: After 6 hours, at midnight, the door opens and the binding fails. If Ukhraalesh has neither fallen nor been driven back 10 rounds later, it breaks out over Ironmere, and in the morning everyone who slept with an amulet around their neck is gone.

concept.twist: The name in Erland’s collar is only half the name: Ukhraal. The demon’s whole name, Ukhraalesh, is cast inside the chapel bell. The familiar did not lie; it kept silent about the last syllable, and Erland called his master’s bell a forgery because the familiar said so. Herluf did not fail from weakness; he went in through the door in place of the girl in the circle, and that girl was Yrsa. Tonight Dyre is the gift, just as she was.
hooks: The cleric’s temple has received a letter without a sender from Ironmere: the birds have fallen silent, and the bell on Greytor no longer rings. The cleric is sent with companions to see what a young and frightened hand dares not write plainly.

The wizard has read of Master Herluf of Greytor, whose books vanished with him forty years ago. In learned circles it is said that his pupil, the healer Erland Highfield, still has them and never lets anyone see them.
A fence the rogue knows has bought wedding rings and silver clasps with grave dirt in their hinges from a nervous young man from Ironmere. Someone is selling the jewellery of the dead.

villain.name: Erland Highfield
villain.nature: An ageing wizard and Ironmere’s beloved healer, Herluf’s apprentice forty years ago. He always wears gloves over hands that turned black the night his master vanished, and a little familiar sits like a toad on his shoulder.
villain.want: To finish his master’s work and do what Herluf did not dare: put Ukhraalesh in irons. He believes a bound demon can give him the years it has eaten from the dead, so that he will never die as Herluf did, and he wants to prove that his master was weak.
villain.plan: Seven nights ago he stole the bell’s clapper so that Yrsa cannot ring at midnight. He has fed the carrion in the dovecote with Ironmere’s stolen dead and given the village lead amulets that make their wearers murmur the name in their sleep. At bedtime the village calls; after 4 hours Dyre walks in a trance to the circle as the gift, and after 5 hours the sleepers walk up to Greytor. At midnight Erland speaks the name and closes the collar around the demon’s neck.
villain.weakness: His hubris and his grief. He has never read Herluf’s letter, and if he sees it, he must choose between his pride and the truth. The name in his collar lacks a syllable, and the familiar serves the demon, not him.

cast.name: Erland Highfield
cast.role: the villain, wizard and Ironmere’s healer
cast.where: In his hall in the tower on Greytor, where he receives guests until 4 hours after sunset; after that in the crypt beneath the chapel ruin.

cast.name: Yrsa
cast.role: the old bell-ringer, once Master Herluf’s serving girl
cast.where: By Ironmere’s churchyard, where she strews salt before the empty graves and lives in a hut by the wall. She is convinced that she died forty years ago.

cast.name: Dyre
cast.role: Erland’s apprentice, who wrote the letter without a sender, and the night’s gift
cast.where: In Ironmere at sunset with a basket of amulets; later in the tower on Greytor or with the heroes, and if nobody steps in, in a trance in the circle in the crypt.

cast.name: Einar Woodyard
cast.role: elder of Ironmere and keeper of the inn
cast.where: At the inn in Ironmere, where he defends Erland, who saved his granddaughter from the fever.

cast.name: Herluf
cast.role: Erland’s master, vanished forty years ago
cast.where: Nowhere: his grave behind the chapel ruin is empty, for he went in through the door in the crypt and never came back. His voice survives only in the letter and in the bell.

cast.name: Ukhraalesh
cast.role: the demon behind the door, which Erland knows only as Ukhraal
cast.where: Behind the door in the circle in the crypt beneath the chapel ruin on Greytor; at midnight it steps through.

factions.name: The People of Ironmere
factions.want: To keep their children alive and their healer in the valley.
factions.method: They wear Erland’s amulets, keep silent about the dead the elder let him take, and look askance at strangers.
factions.attitude: Wary of the heroes and loyal to Erland. They change sides if the heroes show them the dovecote or wake a sleeper who has murmured the name.

factions.name: The House on Greytor
factions.want: To complete the summoning at midnight.
factions.method: Erland is courteous and plays for time; the familiar listens unseen and steals whatever could harm the plan; Dyre obeys and doubts.
factions.attitude: Erland receives the heroes as a host and means to keep them talking until midnight. He turns hostile when they touch the anchors.

outline.title: The Silent Birds
outline.purpose: The heroes reach Ironmere at sunset with the letter without a sender. The birds sit silent on every roof; at the inn the elder Einar Woodyard defends the healer on Greytor and calls Yrsa mad. Dyre hands out the last lead amulets, nervously helpful, and offers to guide them up to the tower. Here the heroes can cut an amulet open and compare his hand with the letter’s.

outline.title: The Woman Who Died Forty Years Ago
outline.purpose: In Ironmere’s churchyard Yrsa strews salt before graves that are empty beneath the untouched turf, and as darkness falls, five corpse lights rise above them. Yrsa tells of the night in the crypt, shows the scar left by the iron ring and gives the heroes Herluf’s letter if they promise to stop Erland.

outline.title: The Village That Talks in Its Sleep
outline.purpose: At bedtime all of Ironmere murmurs the half name. The heroes can burn the amulets with Einar’s help once he has seen proof, or slip from house to house in secret. Each burnt amulet wakes its wearer, and when they are all burnt, the call is broken. It costs time they may not have.

outline.title: Greytor in the Dark
outline.purpose: The heroes climb to Greytor, and the birds follow them with their heads. The way in leads through the dovecote, where Ironmere’s dead hang in the dark under the roof, and the oldest wake; here the carrion can be broken. In the chapel ruin the heroes read the whole name in the mute bell and see the rope vanish down into the crypt, and behind the chapel stands Herluf’s empty grave.

outline.title: The Wizard’s House
outline.purpose: If the heroes come before 4 hours have passed, Erland receives them in the hall as a courteous host who means to keep them there; otherwise the house is empty. In the study they find the plan, the journal and the clapper, and the familiar lurks unseen. In the cellar under the dovecote lies Dyre’s diary, and Erland’s own passage to the chapel is guarded by a glyph.

outline.title: The Door in the Crypt
outline.purpose: At midnight the door opens in the circle. Erland speaks the half name, the collar breaks, and Ukhraalesh is free. The anchors the heroes have broken, the clapper in the bell, the whole name and Erland’s own choice decide whether the demon falls, is driven back or breaks out over Ironmere.

locationThemes.name: The Gate of Greytor
locationThemes.purpose: The ring wall and the open gate, where the birds sit thickest and follow the heroes with their heads. Wheel tracks with churchyard earth lead across the yard into the dovecote, the only open door into the house.

locationThemes.name: The Dovecote
locationThemes.purpose: The entrance to Erland’s house and the first anchor, the carrion: high up among the nesting holes, Ironmere’s stolen dead hang on hooks, hidden in the dark above the guests’ heads, and the oldest have woken as ghouls and ghasts. A lead plate with the half name is nailed to the centre post.

locationThemes.name: The Cellar
locationThemes.purpose: Under the dovecote: the workshop where the amulets are cast in lead, and Dyre’s sleeping place with his diary under the pillow.

locationThemes.name: The Tower Hall
locationThemes.purpose: Erland’s receiving room on the tower’s ground floor: patients’ benches, bunches of herbs, a fire that burns blue, and shelves of amulets, each with a label bearing its wearer’s name. Here Erland receives guests until 4 hours after sunset.

locationThemes.name: The Study
locationThemes.purpose: At the top of the tower: Herluf’s books, Erland’s plan and journal, the bell’s clapper as a trophy above the writing desk, and the familiar, listening unseen.

locationThemes.name: The Chapel Ruin
locationThemes.purpose: The roofless chapel in the middle of the house, with the bell tower above the altar. The bell lacks its clapper, and inside its rim stands the whole name. The bell rope hangs down through a hole in the floor into the crypt, and an arch in the east wall leads down there.

locationThemes.name: The Passage
locationThemes.purpose: Erland’s own way: the old passage under the yard from the tower hall to the chapel, with his glyph on the door into the chapel and small claw marks at knee height along the walls from the night forty years ago.

locationThemes.name: Herluf’s Empty Grave
locationThemes.purpose: The small churchyard behind the chapel ruin, reached from the yard around the outside of the chapel. Nobody lies under Herluf’s gravestone; Yrsa has carved a line into the stone and strewn salt around the grave every night for forty years.

locationThemes.name: The Crypt
locationThemes.purpose: Under the chapel’s east end: a long vault where a stair leads down to the circle of iron and salt around the door, with the collar on its chain, the bell rope from the hole in the ceiling and Herluf’s last scratches in the stone. The climax at midnight.

clueMap.conclusion: Erland Highfield will summon a demon at midnight tonight in the crypt beneath the chapel ruin on Greytor, as his master Herluf tried to forty years ago.

clues.observation: The letter without a sender, which the heroes carry, is written in the same young, careful hand as the name labels on the amulets in Dyre’s basket.
clues.inference: The letter comes from Erland’s apprentice in the tower on Greytor, and what he fears will happen before the new moon, which is tonight.
clues.handout:
To whoever still dares to walk against the dark.
In Ironmere the birds have gone silent. They sit on the roofs and look up at Greytor.
The bell has not rung for three nights, and my master says it is an honour.
I do not think it is an honour. Come before the new moon, and ask for her who rang the bell.

clues.observation: Yrsa tells of the night forty years ago: the birds came seven days before, and Master Herluf opened a door in the crypt beneath the chapel while she herself lay in the circle. She has rung the bell every midnight since, until the clapper vanished seven nights ago.
clues.inference: The same thing is happening again in the same place, and only Erland, Herluf’s old apprentice, can be behind it.

clues.observation: The bell rope hangs down through a hole in the floor before the altar. From the dark below rises the smell of hot iron, and a faint blue light flickers down there.
clues.inference: There is a room beneath the chapel, and someone is making it ready tonight.

clues.observation: The door at the end of the passage into the chapel is freshly greased, and a cold draught from the chapel beyond it makes the candles burn blue.
clues.inference: Erland walks the passage from his tower to the chapel and the crypt without anyone seeing him cross the yard.

clueMap.conclusion: The binding will fail: the name in Erland’s collar and on the amulets is only half the name, Ukhraal. The demon’s whole name is Ukhraalesh, and it is cast in the chapel bell.

clues.observation: Cut one of the lead amulets open, and inside lies a strip of parchment with a single word in red ink and Erland’s initials on the back.
clues.inference: The word Ironmere wears around its neck comes from Erland, and it is the same word the village later murmurs in its sleep.
clues.handout:
UKHRAAL
For the health of Ironmere. E.H.

clues.observation: Herluf’s letter with its unbroken seal, which Yrsa has kept for forty years without opening it.
clues.inference: Herluf found out that the name was incomplete, and that no name can bind the demon. The whole name is in the bell, and the bell and the name together can drive it back.
clues.handout:
Erland. The name the little one gave us is only half of it. It did not lie; it kept silent.
The whole name is in the bell. No name binds it. No chain holds it.
The bell with its own clapper and the whole name spoken in the circle can drive it back.
But the door can only be closed from inside, so I am going in. The girl must live. Ring every midnight.
Forgive me, my boy. Herluf

clues.observation: Inside the bell’s rim stands a name in old runes, one syllable longer than the word on the amulets, and beneath it a short line and the letter H.
clues.inference: The bell’s name is the whole one; the amulets’ name is cut short. It is the bell’s name that must be spoken in the circle.
clues.handout:
UKHRAALESH
YOUR NAME IS KNOWN. TURN BACK.
H.

clues.observation: In Erland’s locked drawer lies his journal; the last page was written seven nights ago.
clues.inference: Erland has never believed in the bell’s name, because the familiar told him it was false, and he trusts the half name blindly.
clues.handout:
The little one says the master’s bell bears a false name, laid to fool those who come after.
That explains why he failed. Tonight I have taken the clapper.
The wench shall not disturb the call any more.

clueMap.conclusion: Three anchors hold the door open: the carrion in the dovecote, the call from the amulets in Ironmere and the gift, Dyre, in the circle. Every anchor the heroes break weakens the demon when it comes.

clues.observation: Yrsa pulls her collar aside: around her neck runs an old white scar shaped like a ring. If she sees Dyre’s iron amulet, she screams, for the same kind hung around her neck when she lay in the circle.
clues.inference: The gift wears iron around its neck, and tonight it is Dyre.

clues.observation: Burn a sleeper’s lead amulet, and that sleeper alone stops murmuring, wakes with a gasp and remembers a dream of wings.
clues.inference: The amulets are the call, and the call can be broken, one amulet at a time.

clues.observation: A lead plate is nailed to the centre post of the dovecote among the dead, with the half name and two more words scratched into the lead. Tear it loose, and every bird on Greytor screams at once, the only sound they make all night.
clues.inference: The carrion is an anchor, and it can be broken.

clues.observation: Under Dyre’s pillow in the cellar lies his diary, written in the same hand as the letter without a sender.
clues.inference: Dyre is the gift and does not know it, and the iron amulet will draw him to the circle.
clues.handout:
Master says I am to stand in the circle at his side tonight. It is an honour.
He hung the iron amulet around my neck himself and said I must never take it off.
I dream of birds every night. I have written to someone. I hope they come.

clues.observation: On Erland’s writing desk lies the plan for the night, written in his neat hand.
clues.inference: All three anchors are there: the carrion, the call and the gift. If the heroes break them, the door holds less well.
clues.handout:
Three nails in the door: the carrion in the dovecote, the call from the sleepers, the gift in the circle.
The gift: the boy, who came of his own free will. The iron about his neck until it is time.
Midnight, the dark of the moon: Ukhraal in the iron. The master hesitated. I shall not.

clueMap.conclusion: Erland has taken the bell’s clapper, and it hangs in his study. Without it the bell can neither keep the demon out nor drive it back.

clues.observation: Seven nights ago Yrsa saw Erland’s lantern in the bell tower late in the evening. At midnight the clapper was gone, and since then the bell has given only a dead sound when she struck it with a stone. The next day the birds came.
clues.inference: Erland took the clapper, and that is what let the birds in.

clues.observation: The clapper’s iron loop inside the bell has been sawn through, and fresh iron filings lie on the beam. On the top rung of the ladder lies a fist-sized stone with fresh scratches of bronze.
clues.inference: The clapper was taken with tools, recently, by someone who knew what it meant, and since then someone has struck the bell with a stone.

clues.observation: Above Erland’s writing desk hangs a heavy iron clapper on a new leather strap like a trophy, with saw marks in its eye that match the loop inside the bell.
clues.inference: It is the bell’s clapper, and it can be hung back.

partyMoments.moment: In the crypt the demon goes for whoever speaks the whole name. The fighter can stand as the wall between the claws and the speaker, or drag the unconscious Dyre out of the circle while the demon slashes at them both.

The cleric can give Ironmere’s stolen dead their rest: turn the waking dead in the dovecote, read out the names on the empty graves so the corpse lights find peace, and stop the demon’s poisonous spores with holy water.

The rogue can slip from house to house in sleeping Ironmere and loosen the lead amulets from the necks of murmuring children without waking them, pick Erland’s drawer and spot the glyph on the door into the chapel before it goes off.

The wizard can read the runes inside the bell and see that the name is one syllable longer than on the amulets, find Herluf’s own books and talk with Erland scholar to scholar, the only conversation he listens to.

scenes.title: The Silent Birds
scenes.summary: The heroes reach Ironmere at sunset and see the birds sitting silent on every roof. At the inn the elder Einar Woodyard defends the healer on Greytor and calls Yrsa mad, and Dyre comes by with the last lead amulets. He is nervously helpful, and his hand is the same as the one in the letter without a sender.
scenes.readAloud: The road down into the valley runs between drystone walls, and on every single stone sits a bird. Ironmere huddles around a church and an inn, and the roofs are so thick with crows, rooks and jackdaws that the thatch cannot be seen. There is no wind, no dog barking and no bird calling; only a door slamming somewhere and a child being hushed. Up on the hill above the village stands a grey stone tower with a single lit window, and every bird is looking up at it.
details: The birds do nothing, but they follow every living thing with their heads. Throw a stone, and they take off and settle again. The villagers walk with bowed necks and do not look up.

At the inn the elder Einar Woodyard pours the ale and would rather not talk about the birds. He defends Erland: the healer saved his granddaughter from the fever last winter and takes no money from the poor. Yrsa is mad, he says; she rang the bell on Greytor every midnight for forty years, and now she stands in the churchyard strewing salt.

Everyone in Ironmere wears a small grey lead amulet on a cord around their neck, the children too. Erland has handed them out for nothing since the harvest, and nobody has fallen ill since. People call them healers and will not take them off.

Dyre comes in with a basket of amulets, each with a small label bearing a name. He is seventeen, thin and ink-stained, and around his own neck hangs an amulet of iron, not lead. He is helpful, talks too fast and keeps glancing at the door. He offers to guide the heroes up to Greytor, where his master gladly receives learned guests.
The letter without a sender, which the heroes carry, is written in the same young, careful hand as the name labels on the amulets in Dyre’s basket.
Cut one of the lead amulets open, and inside lies a strip of parchment with a single word in red ink and Erland’s initials on the back.

Confronted with the letter, Dyre goes white and begs them to keep quiet: he wrote it because he is afraid, but he still believes his master is a great man. He does not know that he himself is the gift, and he will not take off the iron amulet, for his master has forbidden it.

If the heroes ask about the dead, Einar looks away. He himself gave Erland leave to take the dead from the churchyard for his studies, in return for medicine for the village; he does not know where they are, and he does not want to know.

checks.success: The heroes see that Einar is ashamed of something to do with the churchyard, and that Dyre is afraid of his master, not of strangers.
checks.failure: Einar seems merely stubborn and Dyre merely shy; the heroes must find their own way to the churchyard.

checks.success: Einar admits that he gave Erland leave to take the dead, and that his own wife, buried last winter, was among them.
checks.failure: Einar grows angry and tells the heroes to leave the healer alone; he will not help them until they show him proof.

checks.success: The word on the strip comes from no human tongue. It is a name, and names like that are not written on amulets for the sake of anyone’s health.
checks.failure: The word makes no sense, but it lodges in the mind and stays there for the rest of the night.

alternatives: Go straight to the churchyard, where Yrsa stands, before the heroes talk to anyone in the village.
Follow Dyre up to Greytor at once; he knows where Yrsa lives but dares not go there himself.
A rogue can find out who has been selling the jewellery of the dead: a girl at the inn has seen Dyre with a purse he should not have.
scenes.dmNotes: Let the birds do the work: describe them every time the heroes step outside, and never let them do anything. Dyre is the key to the whole night; play him likeable and nervous, so the players will want to save him once they understand what the iron amulet means. The clock runs from sunset, so keep track of the time from the first scene.

scenes.title: The Woman Who Died Forty Years Ago
scenes.summary: In Ironmere’s churchyard Yrsa strews salt before the graves that are empty beneath the untouched turf, and as darkness falls, five corpse lights rise above them. Yrsa tells of the night in the crypt, shows the scar left by the iron ring and gives the heroes Herluf’s letter if they promise to stop Erland.
scenes.readAloud: The churchyard lies just behind the church, and the snow on it is white and untouched, except for one long line of salt before a row of new graves. A small, stooped woman in a grey cloak walks along the line, sprinkling more salt from a leather pouch and counting softly to herself. As the last light fades behind the hills, small, cold lights kindle above the graves, one by one, and hang quietly a foot above the ground.
details: Twelve graves from the last two winters have untouched turf, but push a knife in, and there is barely a foot of earth above empty coffins. The turf has been cut and laid neatly back.

Yrsa is small and stooped, with white hair and nails grey with salt. She is convinced that she died forty years ago and speaks of herself in the past tense: “I was a serving girl on Greytor.” She does not eat, and she thanks no one for anything.

Yrsa tells of the night forty years ago: the birds came seven days before, and Master Herluf opened a door in the crypt beneath the chapel while she herself lay in the circle. She has rung the bell every midnight since, until the clapper vanished seven nights ago.
Yrsa pulls her collar aside: around her neck runs an old white scar shaped like a ring. If she sees Dyre’s iron amulet, she screams, for the same kind hung around her neck when she lay in the circle.

Herluf’s letter with its unbroken seal, which Yrsa has kept for forty years without opening it. She would never break the seal, and she never dared take the letter up to Erland; she gives it only to someone who promises to stop him.

Seven nights ago Yrsa saw Erland’s lantern in the bell tower late in the evening. At midnight the clapper was gone, and since then the bell has given only a dead sound when she struck it with a stone. The next day the birds came.
Yrsa knows that Dyre has dug up the dead; she has seen him with the cart at night. She says it without anger: “He is a gift. Gifts do as they are told.”
The corpse lights are the souls of the stolen dead. They cannot find rest because their bodies do not lie in the earth, and they cannot cross Yrsa’s line of salt (see the hazard).

checks.success: The heroes understand that Yrsa is not mad; she holds on to one thing so as not to fall apart, and that thing is the bell. She gives them the letter at once.
checks.failure: Yrsa demands that the heroes swear by something they hold sacred before she gives them the letter; it costs 10 minutes and an oath she will remind them of.

checks.success: The heroes know the rite for the dead without a grave: read their names aloud at their graves and promise to bring them home, and the corpse lights grow calm and drift up towards Greytor, as if showing the way.
checks.failure: The heroes do not know the rite. Yrsa knows the names by heart, but she needs time, so it lasts the whole fight.

checks.success: The turf was cut with a spade with a notch in its blade; the same spade lies on Erland’s cart up on Greytor.
checks.failure: The heroes see only that the turf has been cut and laid neatly back.

creatures.name: Corpse lights over the empty graves

encounter.tactics: The five corpse lights rise when the last daylight is gone and go for living creatures that stand on the graves or try to dig in them. They use Vanish to turn invisible and reappear beside whoever stands alone before attacking with Shock; if a living creature drops to 0 HP, they try to use Consume Life. They do not leave the churchyard and do not cross Yrsa’s line of salt (see the hazard). If they grow calm (see the checks), they drift away up towards Greytor and do not come back tonight.
encounter.terrain: The churchyard is snow-covered and full of leaning gravestones that give Half Cover. It is dark; the corpse lights’ own glow is the only light until they use Vanish. Yrsa’s line of salt runs in front of the twelve empty graves.
encounter.hazard: The Salt Line. When: all night. Targets: the corpse lights. Save: none. Effect: the corpse lights cannot cross Yrsa’s unbroken line of salt, so whoever stands behind it is safe from them. Counter: if the salt is scuffed aside in one place, they can get through there.

alternatives: Step behind Yrsa’s line of salt and talk with her there; the corpse lights cannot reach the heroes, but they hover close enough to show what they are.
Read the names of the dead aloud and promise to bring them home (see the checks); then the corpse lights drift towards Greytor and show the way to the dovecote.
Leave the graves alone; the corpse lights go only for those who stand on them.
scenes.dmNotes: Yrsa is the heart of the adventure. Play her quiet, certain and without self-pity: she believes she is dead and has only the bell left. She need not explain everything; the letter does the rest. If the heroes have Dyre with them, her scream at the sight of the iron amulet is the night’s first real chill. The corpse lights need not become a fight; they are a sign of what has happened to the dead.

scenes.title: The Village That Talks in Its Sleep
scenes.summary: At bedtime all of Ironmere murmurs the half name in its sleep. The heroes can burn the amulets with Einar’s help once he has seen proof, or slip from house to house in secret. Each burnt amulet wakes its wearer, and when they are all burnt, the call is broken.
scenes.readAloud: Ironmere has gone to bed, but the village is not quiet. Behind every closed shutter a voice murmurs, low and even, the same word over and over, and the voices fall into step until the whole village sounds as if it were breathing as one. On the roofs the birds turn their heads after the sound, slowly, as if they were a single creature. From a window behind the inn comes a child’s voice, murmuring along.
details: From 2 hours after sunset, everyone who sleeps with one of Erland’s lead amulets around their neck murmurs the half name, Ukhraal. They cannot be shaken awake.

Burn a sleeper’s lead amulet, and that sleeper alone stops murmuring, wakes with a gasp and remembers a dream of wings. An amulet that is torn off must go into a fire within a minute, or its wearer starts murmuring again.

With Einar: if the heroes show him proof (the brooch from his wife, an empty grave, Herluf’s letter or his own granddaughter murmuring the name), he goes from house to house with them, wakes the families and has them throw the amulets onto a bonfire in the square before the inn. It takes 1 hour.
In secret: the heroes slip into the sleeping houses, take the amulets from the necks of murmuring people, children too, and burn them in the inn’s kitchen fire. It takes 2 hours.

The call is broken when the amulets in every house in Ironmere have been burnt (see the Door and the Three Anchors in the Crypt). Every house the heroes skip keeps the call alive, and its people walk up to Greytor after 5 hours.

Einar’s granddaughter, a girl of seven, murmurs loudest of all. He sits by her bed with his hand around the amulet and dares not take it off, for it saved her from the fever, he believes. If he takes it off himself, he is won over to the heroes.
A villager who has been woken remembers only wings and a big grey bird sitting on their chest, and is afraid to fall asleep again.
After 5 hours the sleepers who still wear amulets rise and walk up the road to Greytor (see the clock). They put up no resistance, but they cannot be woken until their amulet is burnt.

checks.success: Einar believes the heroes and wakes the village with them; the amulets are burnt within 1 hour, and people thank them afterwards.
checks.failure: Einar wants to see proof with his own eyes; the heroes must fetch something from Greytor or show him his own granddaughter murmuring.

checks.success: The heroes gather the amulets from the whole village in 2 hours without anyone waking before their amulet burns.
checks.failure: A family wakes and cries out about thieves; the heroes must talk their way out or flee, and it costs 30 minutes more.

checks.success: The villagers hand over their amulets out of fear; it goes quickly (1 hour), but nobody will help the heroes afterwards.
checks.failure: The villagers gather around the inn with axes and pitchforks. They do not fight, but they do not move aside either, and the heroes must try another way.

alternatives: Split the party: some burn amulets with Einar while others go up to Greytor; the clock runs for both.
Skip the village and go straight for the tower; the call then still stands, and the sleepers come up to the chapel after 5 hours.
Take only the amulets from the houses nearest the road; that saves their people, but the call is not broken.
scenes.dmNotes: This is the night’s most expensive choice: every hour in the village is an hour the heroes do not have on Greytor. Let the murmuring be loudest just outside the windows, and let a child murmur along. If the heroes sneak, describe the sleeping faces turning towards them in the dark without waking. A broken call makes the demon weaker at midnight; do not say so, but let the players feel that they have done something that matters.

scenes.title: Greytor in the Dark
scenes.summary: The heroes climb to Greytor, where the birds follow them with their heads. The way in leads through the dovecote, where Ironmere’s dead hang in the dark under the roof, and the oldest wake when the heroes touch them or the lead plate. In the chapel ruin the heroes can read the whole name in the mute bell, and behind the chapel stands Herluf’s empty grave.
scenes.readAloud: The road from Ironmere up the hill is steep and slick with rime, and the birds sit close on every fence and every branch. At the ring wall the house on Greytor lies dark before you: a square dovecote, a tower with a single lit window and behind them a chapel without a roof, its bell tower black against the stars. The smell of juniper smoke and of something sweet and rotten drifts down towards you on the cold air.
details: The road up takes 30 minutes. From the gate there is only one open door into the house: the dovecote’s cart door (see the Gate of Greytor).

In the dovecote the dead hang high up, and guests do not see them without a light. If the heroes touch the centre post or the lead plate, or climb onto the gallery, the oldest dead wake (see the Dovecote).
If the heroes come before 4 hours have passed, Erland waits in the tower hall and hears them coming; Dyre or the familiar has told him (see the Wizard’s House).
In the chapel ruin the bell hangs mute, for the clapper is gone. Inside the rim stands the whole name (see the Chapel Ruin).
The wheel tracks and the cart show that the dead were brought up here from Ironmere, and the spade on the cart has a notch in its blade.

If the call has not been broken, Ironmere’s sleepers come up the road after 5 hours and stand silent around the chapel. They do nothing, but they stand in the way, and none of them wakes until their amulet is burnt.
If the heroes break the carrion, every bird on Greytor screams at once and then falls silent again; Erland hears it wherever he is.

checks.success: The heroes see the dead on the gallery before they touch anything and can choose how to go about it.
checks.failure: The heroes walk in under the dead without seeing them; if the dead wake, the heroes have Disadvantage on their Initiative.

checks.success: The heroes read the tracks: a young man in narrow boots has dragged the dead from the cart into the dovecote over many nights, and an old woman walks along the chapel wall to the churchyard every night.
checks.failure: The tracks have been trampled by birds and snow, and the heroes must search on their own (10 minutes for each place).

checks.success: The heroes climb the centre post or the ladder in one go and reach the lead plate before the dead are down.
checks.failure: The ladder creaks and slips, and the climber gets only halfway up in the first round.

alternatives: Set fire to the dovecote from outside with lamp oil; after 10 minutes the fire has taken hold and the carrion is broken, but the dead who wake come out through the cart door, and Erland knows at once what has happened.
Go round the dovecote along the path by the chapel wall to the churchyard, and climb into the chapel ruin over the low wall (see Herluf’s Empty Grave).
Let Dyre lead them in: he walks through the dovecote without looking up and takes them to the hall.
scenes.dmNotes: Greytor should feel like a house holding its breath. Play the dovecote slowly: the smell, the drop, the creaking, and let the players look up for themselves. If time is short, remind them of the clock in the hall or of the birds turning their heads. The chapel is the night’s quiet revelation: the whole name in the bell should feel like a key they found themselves.

scenes.title: The Wizard’s House
scenes.summary: If the heroes come before 4 hours have passed, Erland receives them in the tower hall as a courteous host who means to keep them there until midnight; otherwise the house is empty. In the study the heroes find the plan, the journal and the clapper, and the familiar lurks unseen. In the cellar under the dovecote lies Dyre’s diary, and Erland’s own passage to the chapel is guarded by a glyph.
scenes.readAloud: A tall, thin man in grey rises from the chair by the blue fire. He wears thin leather gloves and has a narrow, kindly face with eyes that take no part in the smile, and on his shoulder sits a grey toad that does not blink. “Welcome to Greytor,” he says, and names you, one by one. “I have been expecting you. The food is getting cold.”
details: Before 4 hours have passed, Erland welcomes the heroes by name; the familiar has been listening, and he knows one thing about each of them. He is courteous, learned and a little tired, and he wants them to eat and talk until the hour is late. He does not lie about his work; he embellishes it: “I am finishing my master’s work. He hesitated. I do not.”

Erland denies knowing anything about the dead and calls Yrsa a poor mad old woman. If the heroes show him Herluf’s letter, he falls silent and pale and wants to read it alone, while the familiar whispers that Yrsa wrote it herself. Even now he cannot stop the door, for the anchors hold it, but the letter can make him choose differently in the crypt (see the Crypt).
If the heroes attack him, he uses the Mage stat block (see the Crypt): Misty Step and Invisibility, and then down the passage to the circle. He will not die for his house, only for the circle.
Once 4 hours have passed, the house is empty: Erland is in the crypt, and the table stands untouched. The longcase clock shows the time.
The study at the top of the tower holds the plan, the journal and the clapper (see the Study). The familiar follows the heroes unseen and tries to steal Herluf’s letter if one of them carries it.
The cellar under the dovecote holds Dyre’s diary and the moulds for the amulets (see the Cellar).

Erland’s own way to the chapel is the passage behind the open arch in the hall’s north wall; the door at its end bears his glyph (see the Passage). The oak door in the hall’s north wall leads straight into the chapel ruin, but it is locked.

If Dyre is with the heroes when 4 hours have passed and still wears the iron amulet, he stops in the middle of a sentence and walks towards the chapel. He puts up no resistance, but he cannot be woken; tear the amulet off him, and he collapses and wakes.

checks.success: The heroes see that Erland cares for no one in the valley, not even Dyre. He is afraid of dying and even more afraid of having wasted forty years, and his pride is the only thing holding him up.
checks.failure: Erland seems merely a courteous, slightly tired scholar, and the heroes stay seated 30 minutes longer than they meant to.

checks.success: The heroes recognise Herluf’s hand from the books in the study and can prove to Erland that the letter is genuine; that gives Advantage when they later try to persuade him.
checks.failure: The heroes cannot prove that the letter is genuine, and the familiar whispers to Erland that Yrsa wrote it.

checks.success: Erland believes the heroes have come to learn from him and shows them the study himself, where the clapper hangs.
checks.failure: Erland smiles and thanks them for the visit; he has the familiar follow them out, and it will try to steal the letter.

alternatives: While one or two heroes talk with Erland in the hall, the others can climb the spiral stair to the study.
Let Dyre show the way to the study and the cellar; he knows where everything is, but not what the plan means for him.
Offer Erland a conversation scholar to scholar: the wizard can get him to answer honestly about names and bindings, because he cannot resist showing what he knows.
scenes.dmNotes: Erland should be the most courteous person in the adventure and the most frightening, because he is completely calm. Let him know the heroes’ names and one detail about each of them. His weapon is time: every question he asks is five more minutes. If the heroes get him to read Herluf’s letter, play his silence long, and let the familiar whisper into it. If the heroes come after 4 hours, read the description of the empty hall instead (see the Tower Hall).

scenes.title: The Door in the Crypt
scenes.summary: At midnight the door opens in the circle in the crypt. Erland speaks the half name and closes the collar around the demon’s neck, but the collar breaks, and Ukhraalesh is free; its first prey is Erland unless someone steps in. The anchors the heroes have broken, the clapper in the bell, the whole name and Erland’s own choice decide whether the demon falls, is driven back or breaks out over Ironmere.
scenes.readAloud: The blue light in the crypt goes out all at once. In the middle of the circle the darkness opens like an eye, and out of it rises something large and hunched, with a vulture’s bare grey neck, long arms with hooks for hands and wings like torn, tanned hide. The stench of a slaughterhouse on a summer’s day fills the crypt, and a sound like a thousand wings beats against the vault. The iron collar closes around its neck with a click and springs in two with a crack like a snapping bone.
details: The objective is resolved here: by force, by the counter-rite or by a sacrifice through the door (see the objective). What the broken anchors take from the demon is set out under the Door and the Three Anchors (see the Crypt); write down its HP before the fight begins.

In rounds 1 and 2 Erland shouts the half name, Ukhraal, again and again and still believes in it. Ukhraalesh laughs inside the heroes’ heads and goes for him first, unless a hero speaks the whole name; then it goes for the speaker.
The counter-rite needs the clapper hanging in the bell. If it has not been hung, a hero can run up into the bell tower with it, but that takes 10 minutes, and the fight does not wait.

Erland’s choice: if the heroes have given him Herluf’s letter, they can get him to walk in through the door himself, as Herluf did (see the checks); it costs him his life and closes the door at once. Without the letter he flees invisible up the stair when the collar breaks.

Yrsa comes up to the chapel at midnight, as she has done for forty years. If the clapper hangs in the bell, she rings from the chapel floor, so the heroes in the crypt have their hands free. If she comes down into the crypt, she walks towards the circle with her hands held out; she wants to go in through the door to Herluf, for she is already dead, she says, and the heroes must choose whether to let her.
If Dyre lies in the circle, he breathes in time with the wingbeats, and the demon regains HP until he is dragged out (see the Crypt).

Ukhraalesh speaks only inside the heroes’ heads, with the voices of their own dead. It promises each of them what they miss most if they let it go; it does not lie, but it keeps silent about the price.

If the demon has neither fallen nor been driven back after 10 rounds, it breaks up through the bell shaft and flies towards Ironmere (see the endings). If the sleepers stand around the chapel, they are the first it reaches.

checks.success: Erland reads Herluf’s letter one last time, pulls off his gloves and walks in through the door with the whole name on his lips. The door closes behind him and takes the demon with it.
checks.failure: Erland clings to his pride and flees, and the heroes must deal with the demon on their own.

checks.success: The heroes drag Dyre out of the circle, and the demon stops regaining HP.
checks.failure: The iron amulet holds Dyre fast; the heroes can try again next round, within the demon’s reach.

checks.success: The heroes hear Erland’s cloak and footsteps as he turns invisible and can stop him on the stair.
checks.failure: Erland is gone and does not show himself again until the fight is over.

alternatives: Let the demon take Erland, and use the rounds it spends on him to hang the clapper or drag Dyre out.
Let Yrsa or Erland go in through the door; it closes at once, but someone pays with their life.
Speak the whole name into the broken collar: the demon is Restrained for one round before it tears itself free and laughs. Herluf was right; no name binds it.
scenes.dmNotes: Go through the anchors for yourself before you read aloud: what have the heroes broken, where is Dyre, and do they have the clapper and the letter? Let the first two rounds be about Erland shouting his half name at a demon that laughs; that is hubris falling. Keep the 10 rounds visible, for example with ten coins on the table. If the fight is too hard, let Yrsa walk towards the circle; if it is too easy, let the demon turn on whoever is ringing.

locations.name: The Gate of Greytor
locations.readAloud: The ring wall around Greytor is black with birds. They sit shoulder to shoulder along the top of the wall, on the beam of the gate and in the bare ash tree in the middle of the yard, and hundreds of heads turn after you without a sound. The yard smells of frozen earth and of something sweet and rotten that comes from the square stone building straight ahead, where a cart stands with black earth caked around its wheels.
locations.description: The ring wall is ten feet high and has only one gate, and it stands open. The buildings of the house hang together inside the wall: the dovecote straight ahead of the gate, the tower to the right and the chapel ruin behind, its bell tower rising above the dovecote’s roof. The tower’s old door to the yard has been bricked up, so the dovecote’s wide cart door is the only open way into the house (see the Dovecote). The birds do nothing, whatever the heroes do; they follow every living thing with their eyes and move aside for no one. The cart is Erland’s; Dyre has driven the dead up from Ironmere in it. A narrow path runs between the ring wall and the chapel wall round to the small churchyard behind the chapel (see Herluf’s Empty Grave).
features: The cart by the cart door: its wheels are caked with greasy black churchyard earth, and on its bed lie a scrap of shroud with the cross of Ironmere’s church embroidered in the corner and a spade with a notch in its blade.

The birds: crows, rooks and jackdaws in their thousands. Throw something at them, and they take off for a moment and settle again at once in the same place. Whoever watches them for long notices that none of them ever blinks.
The tower’s old door to the yard has been bricked up with new stones and has not been used for years.
The path along the chapel wall to the churchyard: in the snow runs a single line of small, dragging footprints, there and back, from last night.
locations.secret: If the heroes stand still in the gateway for a minute, they see that the birds stop watching them as long as they do not move: every beak points at the same spot, the east end of the chapel ruin, where the crypt lies.

locations.name: The Dovecote
locations.readAloud: The cart door opens into a tall, square room of limestone whose walls are pitted like a beehive with nesting holes all the way up to the rafters. It smells of juniper smoke from an iron brazier by the door, and beneath the smoke of something sweet and fatty that settles at the back of the throat. Far up in the dark something creaks slowly back and forth, and every now and then a drop falls onto the stone floor.
locations.description: The dovecote is Erland’s entrance hall: everyone who comes in from the yard passes through here, beneath the dead, without seeing them. The room is 40 feet high; 25 feet up, a timber gallery runs all the way round, carried by a thick centre post of oak, and two ladders lead up to it. On the gallery twelve of Ironmere’s dead from the last two winters hang on hooks between the nesting holes, wrapped in their shrouds, and the birds feed on them in silence. This is the carrion, the first of the three anchors: the scent that shows the demon the way. The anchor is broken when the lead plate on the centre post has been torn loose and smashed, or when the dead have been burnt (see the Door and the Three Anchors in the Crypt). To the west a low door leads down to the cellar, to the east an open arch leads to the tower hall, and to the north-east an open arch leads into the chapel ruin.
features: The lead plate: a lead plate is nailed to the centre post of the dovecote among the dead, up by the gallery, with the half name and two more words scratched into the lead. It can be reached from the gallery or by climbing the post (DC 13 Strength (Athletics)), and it is torn loose with a DC 13 Strength check or smashed (AC 10, 5 HP). Tear it loose, and every bird on Greytor screams at once, the only sound they make all night.

The dead: twelve wrapped figures on the gallery. The shrouds bear Ironmere’s cross in the corner, and several of the dead still wear rings and brooches. One of them wears a green wedding dress and a silver brooch shaped like a sheaf of corn: the wife of Einar Woodyard, the elder, buried last winter. The brooch is the proof that makes Einar believe the heroes.
The iron brazier of smouldering juniper by the cart door, with a bucket of fresh twigs beside it: the smoke is there to hide the stench from guests.
The tracks on the floor: drag marks of shrouds from the cart door to the ladders, and the footprints of narrow boots, a young man’s.
The birds in the nesting holes, hundreds of them, silent. They feed only when no light falls on them.

encounter.tactics: The dead wake when a living creature sets foot on the gallery, touches the centre post or the lead plate, or makes a noise in here. They climb down the ladders and the post and go for the nearest living creature. The two oldest, black and bloated, keep together and go for whoever stands by the post; the newest crowd around whoever stands alone. They never flee, and they follow no one out of the dovecote. If a living creature drops to 0 HP, two of the newest try to drag the body up onto the gallery instead of fighting on.
encounter.terrain: The gallery 25 feet up has no railing; anyone pushed over the edge falls and takes 2d6 Bludgeoning damage. The ladders are Difficult Terrain. The hanging bodies swing when someone passes them and give Half Cover on the gallery. The stone floor is slick with droppings and grease.
encounter.hazard: Bird Storm. When: the first time someone tears the lead plate loose or sets fire to the dead. Targets: everyone in the dovecote. Save: none. Effect: hundreds of birds burst from the nesting holes and whirl about, and the whole dovecote is Heavily Obscured until the end of the next round. Counter: leave through the cart door or one of the arches, or wait a round.

treasure: The jewellery of the dead: rings, brooches and clasps worth about 140 gp in all. They belong to Ironmere’s families, and if the heroes take them, the village turns against them.
locations.secret: Behind a loose stone in a nesting hole by the east ladder, Dyre has hidden a purse with 34 gp, the payment from a fence in the city for the jewellery he has already sold, and a scrap with the fence’s address in his own hand.

locations.name: The Cellar
locations.readAloud: The stair from the dovecote ends in a low cellar where a row of thick pillars carries the vault. The air is warm and dry and tastes of metal; behind the pillars a forge glows beneath a casting ladle, and along the wall stand crates full of small grey amulets. In the farthest corner a bed has been made up for one on a straw mattress beneath a shelf of books.
locations.description: Here Erland and Dyre cast the amulets: lead is melted in the forge and poured into a mould bearing Erland’s mark, a hand around a key, and into each amulet goes a strip of parchment with the half name, written by Erland himself in red ink. The crates hold about three hundred finished amulets, but it is the ones around the necks of Ironmere’s sleepers that call (see the scene where the village talks in its sleep). Dyre sleeps down here; he only goes up into the tower when he is called. The cellar has only one way out, the door up to the dovecote.
features: Under Dyre’s pillow in the cellar lies his diary, written in the same young, careful hand as the letter without a sender.
The moulds: the lead mould with Erland’s mark for the village’s amulets and a smaller mould of iron, in which Dyre’s iron amulet was cast. It is older than anything else down here.
The crates: about three hundred identical lead amulets. Cut one open, and the strip with the half name lies inside.
The forge is still warm; the last amulet was cast yesterday.
Dyre’s shelf: a herbal, a worn grammar of old runes with his own small comments in the margins, and a children’s book about birds. Dyre can read the runes in the bell if someone shows them to him.
treasure: A small bar of silver that Erland uses to silver his finest amulets (25 gp).
locations.secret: In a crack behind the forge lies an old iron amulet with a burst chain and the word UKHRAAL scratched into it: the one Yrsa wore as the gift forty years ago. Erland has kept it all these years and used it as the model for Dyre’s.

locations.name: The Tower Hall
locations.readAloud: The tower’s ground floor is a long hall with two rows of whitewashed pillars, patients’ benches along the walls and bunches of herbs hanging from the beams to dry. In the great fireplace burns a fire with blue flames that give no warmth, and before it stands a table laid for guests: four plates, four cups and a carafe of dark wine. From wall to wall stand shelves with hundreds of small hooks, each beneath a paper label with a name, and nearly all the hooks are empty. Behind the shelves a longcase clock ticks, loud and slow.
locations.description: Here Erland receives the sick and his guests, and here he waits for the heroes until 4 hours after sunset (see the Wizard’s House). The table is laid because the familiar has told him they are coming. The shelves are his register: each amulet hangs under a label with a villager’s name and a date, and where a hook is empty, that villager already wears their amulet; nearly all of Ironmere does. The blue fire is the first sign that the door is wearing thin. The oak door to the north leads straight into the chapel ruin and is locked, and the open arch to the north leads down into Erland’s own passage to the chapel (see the Passage). A spiral stair in the corner climbs to the study, and the arch to the west leads out to the dovecote.
features: The register: each amulet on the shelves hangs under a label with a name and a date in Dyre’s hand. Only nine are left, and by every empty hook there is a small cross.
The longcase clock by the spiral stair shows the true time of the night; the heroes can keep track of the time here.
The fireplace: the fire burns blue and gives no warmth. Whoever holds a hand in it feels only cold.

The locked oak door to the chapel ruin: Erland carries the key on a cord around his neck. It is picked with a DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check using thieves’ tools or forced open with a DC 17 Strength check.
The cabinet of salves and draughts for the sick stands unlocked by the patients’ benches.
The table is laid for four with wine, bread and cold venison. The food is good and the wine is clean; Erland only wants his guests to stay seated.
treasure: Three Potions of Healing in small clay jars in the cabinet, brewed by Erland for the village’s sick (50 gp each).
locations.secret: Behind the fireplace’s iron fireback there is a small niche with Herluf’s silver handbell, cast from the same metal as the chapel bell. Erland has hidden it for forty years because he could not bring himself to melt it down.

locations.name: The Study
locations.readAloud: At the top of the tower the spiral stair opens into a round chamber under steep rafters. Books stand in piles from floor to ceiling, the windows are covered with black cloth, and a single candle burns blue on the writing desk. Above the desk hangs a heavy iron clapper on a leather strap, and behind it the wall is covered with the same word in chalk, over and over, a thousand times.
locations.description: Herluf’s old library and Erland’s study. Here Erland has practised the half name for forty years; the wall behind the desk is covered with the word UKHRAAL. The plan for the night lies on the desk, the journal in the locked drawer and the clapper above the desk. The familiar keeps watch here, unseen, when Erland is below (see the fight). The clapper weighs 30 pounds and can be carried by one person; it fits the loop inside the bell, and hanging it takes 10 minutes on the ladder in the chapel ruin.
features: On Erland’s writing desk lies the plan for the night, written in his neat hand.

In Erland’s locked drawer lies his journal; the last page was written seven nights ago. The drawer is picked with a DC 13 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check using thieves’ tools or forced with a DC 15 Strength check.
Above Erland’s writing desk hangs a heavy iron clapper on a new leather strap like a trophy, with saw marks in its eye that match the loop inside the bell.
Herluf’s books on the top shelves, each marked with the letter H on its spine, among them his black-bound spellbook.
The wall of chalk: UKHRAAL in Erland’s hand, a thousand times.
A glass cage with damp moss and a saucer of milk: the familiar’s bed.

encounter.tactics: The familiar is only 1 quasit, and it does not fight if it can avoid it. It follows the heroes unseen, steals or destroys Herluf’s letter if it can get at it, and whispers to Erland through the walls. If it is discovered, it uses Scare on the nearest creature and escapes as a bat or a centipede. If it is caught, it bargains: it offers the demon’s name but gives only half of it until it is pressed with a DC 15 Charisma (Intimidation) check.
encounter.terrain: The piles of books topple if anyone runs between them, and the windows are covered, so it is dark here except for the blue candle.

treasure: Herluf’s spellbook bound in black leather, with Magic Circle, Remove Curse, Dispel Magic, Counterspell, Glyph of Warding and Banishment; a wizard can copy them into their own book once they can prepare spells of those levels.
An iron-bound chest under the desk with 260 gp and six garnets worth 50 gp each, payment from the valley’s sick over twenty years.
Herluf’s grey woollen cloak on a peg behind the door, which Erland has never touched: a Cloak of Protection.
locations.secret: In the moss of the familiar’s cage lies a burnt scrap of paper bearing Herluf’s H, the only piece of his writing it has ever found. It has been searching for the letter he wrote that night for forty years.

locations.name: The Chapel Ruin
locations.readAloud: The chapel has no roof; snow and starlight fall in between two rows of sooty pillars, and between them fallen roof tiles lie in heaps. Above the altar at the east end rises a narrow bell tower with a great bronze bell that hangs perfectly still, and a thick rope runs from it down through a hole in the floor before the altar. Beside the altar a low arch leads down into darkness, and from there rises a faint smell of hot iron.
locations.description: The chapel’s roof burned the night Herluf vanished and was never laid again. The bell tower above the altar is reached by a 30-foot ladder. The bell is Herluf’s; inside its rim stands the whole name, and its clapper is gone (see the Study). The rope runs from the bell down through the floor to the circle in the crypt, so it can be rung both from here and from below. Without the clapper the bell gives only a dead sound. With the clapper hung back in place (10 minutes on the ladder) it rings clear, and its sound is one half of the counter-rite (see the Crypt). The arch in the east wall leads down a short stair to the crypt. The door to the north is Erland’s own door from the passage, and the oak door to the south, to the tower hall, is locked. If the call has not been broken, Ironmere’s sleepers stand silent around the chapel after 5 hours.
features: The bell rope hangs down through a hole in the floor before the altar. From the dark below rises the smell of hot iron, and a faint blue light flickers down there.

Inside the bell’s rim stands a name in old runes, one syllable longer than the word on the amulets, and beneath it a short line and the letter H. Anyone who compares it with an amulet cut open sees the difference without a check.
The clapper’s iron loop inside the bell has been sawn through, and fresh iron filings lie on the beam. On the top rung of the ladder lies a fist-sized stone with fresh scratches of bronze.
The altar: a block of limestone with a clean white cloth and a bowl of salt, which Yrsa sets out every night.
The pillars are black with soot up to a man’s height from the fire, and someone has scratched small crosses into the soot.
locations.secret: Beside the hole for the rope sits a loose floor tile. Under it is a spyhole down into the crypt, through which the circle, the collar and, once 4 hours have passed, Erland and Dyre can be seen.

locations.name: The Passage
locations.readAloud: The passage is a broad, low vault under the yard, so low that a tall man must bow his head. The walls are covered with small, parallel scratches at knee height, thousands of them, as if from the claws of something small that has run along them again and again. At the end towards the chapel stands an iron door, freshly greased and shining, and the air around it is so cold that your breath hangs white.
locations.description: Herluf had the passage dug so that he could walk from the tower to the chapel without crossing the yard, and Erland uses it every night. The scratches are the familiar’s; it has run here for forty years. The door into the chapel bears Erland’s glyph (see the trap). If the word Ukhraal is spoken aloud at the door before it is opened, the glyph does not go off. Erland says it every time, and Dyre knows it. The open arch at the other end leads back to the tower hall.
features: The door at the end of the passage into the chapel is freshly greased, and a cold draught from the chapel beyond it makes the candles burn blue.
The claw marks at knee height along both walls; some of them are fresh.
A small copper plate by the door with the word UKHRAAL scratched into it in Erland’s hand: his reminder for Dyre, so that the boy can pass the glyph.
Footprints in the dust from soft shoes, back and forth, many times.
locations.trap: Erland’s glyph (Glyph of Warding) on the passage side of the door into the chapel. It goes off when the door is opened by anyone who has not spoken the word Ukhraal aloud at the door, and it explodes in a sphere with a 20-foot radius: everyone in the sphere makes a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw and takes 22 (5d8) Thunder damage on a failure or half as much on a success, and the blast can be heard throughout the house and down in the crypt. The glyph is found with a DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) check as an almost invisible spiral of silver lines around the lock, and it is defused with the word or with Dispel Magic.
locations.secret: Halfway along the passage a stone in the ceiling is loose. Behind it the familiar has gathered a black feather, a scrap of Herluf’s sleeve and a small silver ring marked with the letter H; it has collected its old master’s things for forty years.

locations.name: Herluf’s Empty Grave
locations.readAloud: Behind the chapel lies a small churchyard with leaning stones and a low drystone wall, half buried in snow. In the middle stands one stone newer than the others, ringed with salt so white that it almost glows in the dark. No birds sit here, and the snow is untouched except for one line of small footprints from the path and back again.
locations.description: Herluf’s gravestone stands over an empty grave; he went in through the door, and there was nothing to bury. Yrsa had the stone set and has since carved a line into it herself. She strews salt around the grave every night when she goes up to ring. The birds never settle here, so it is the only place on Greytor where the heroes can take a short rest without being watched. The chapel wall is low here, and they can climb into the chapel ruin with a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check.
features: The gravestone: HERLUF, MASTER OF GREYTOR, and beneath, carved by an unsteady hand: HE CLOSED THE DOOR FROM INSIDE.
The ring of salt around the grave is fresh from last night.
The other graves belong to servants and farmers from Greytor’s old days; all of them are more than forty years old.
locations.secret: If someone digs the grave up, they find an empty coffin with a single black feather, as long as a forearm, that never grows warm in the hand. It was torn from Ukhraalesh the night the door was closed.

locations.name: The Crypt
locations.readAloud: The stair from the chapel ends in a long, low vault whose ceiling is black with soot and where white feathers hang caught in the cobwebs. At the far end a broad stair leads down into a round pit, where a circle of iron and salt is set into the floor around a patch of darkness that the light of your lanterns cannot reach into. Above the circle a black iron collar hangs on a chain from the ceiling, and beside it the bell rope hangs down through a hole in the vault. The air tastes of iron and burnt feathers, and from the darkness comes a sound like a thousand wings far away.
locations.description: Herluf had the crypt hewn beneath the chapel’s east end for his summoning, and here he closed the door from inside. The circle is 20 feet across and lies down in the pit; in its middle is the door, a patch of darkness that cannot be lit. The bell rope hangs down into the circle, so whoever stands in it can ring. From 4 hours after sunset Erland stands here with the collar, and if Dyre still wears his iron amulet, he lies in the circle as the gift, in a trance. At midnight the door opens by the rules in the hazard below; Erland speaks the half name and closes the collar around the demon’s neck, and the collar breaks. From then on Ukhraalesh is free, and the heroes have 10 rounds. The objective is resolved here: by force, by the counter-rite or by a sacrifice through the door (see the objective).
features: The circle: a ring of wrought iron sunk into the stone floor with a thick band of salt inside it, 20 feet across. The whole name must be spoken inside it.
The collar: black iron, a hand’s breadth wide, with the word UKHRAAL engraved on the inside. At midnight it breaks with a crack like a snapping bone.
The bell rope hangs from the hole in the vault down into the circle; whoever pulls it rings the bell in the chapel above.
The pit: nine steps lead down to the circle from the vault. The edge is 10 feet high, and the vault above the pit is 30 feet high.

Dyre in the circle, if he has not been saved: he lies on his back with open eyes and breathes in time with the wingbeats. Dragging him out takes a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check as an action, for the iron amulet holds him fast.

encounter.tactics: Before midnight Erland fights only if the heroes attack him or touch the circle; then he uses Arcane Burst and Fireball to keep them away and Shield and Misty Step to stay by the circle. At midnight he shouts the half name for two rounds and still believes in it. Ukhraalesh goes for Erland first, unless a hero speaks the whole name; then it goes for the speaker and does not let go. It uses Spores when three or more stand within 20 feet, Stunning Screech once, when it can catch the most, and flies up under the vault to get above whoever is ringing. It speaks only inside the heroes’ heads, with the voices of their own dead. When the collar breaks, Erland flees invisible up the stair, unless the heroes have given him Herluf’s letter; then a DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check can make him walk in through the door himself, as his master did.
encounter.terrain: The vault is low (10 feet), but above the pit it rises to 30 feet, so the demon can fly in there. The stair down into the pit is Difficult Terrain, and from the edge of the pit one can see down into the circle and strike with ranged weapons.
encounter.hazard: The Door and the Three Anchors. When: at midnight, when the door opens, and until the demon falls, is driven back or breaks out after 10 rounds. Targets: Ukhraalesh. Save: none. Effect: until the 10 rounds have passed, it cannot leave the crypt, and every anchor broken by midnight takes something from it. Carrion broken (the lead plate in the dovecote smashed or the dead burnt): it has 102 HP instead of 152. Call broken (Ironmere’s amulets burnt): it cannot use Stunning Screech. Gift broken (Dyre is not in the circle at midnight): it cannot fly and cannot leave the circle for the first 2 rounds. If Dyre lies in the circle, it regains 10 HP at the start of each of its turns until he is dragged out. If all three anchors are broken, the door opens only if Erland steps into the circle and gives himself as the gift; then the demon comes with all three weaknesses, and Erland is gone. Counter: the counter-rite with the bell and the whole name, or a sacrifice through the door (see the objective).

treasure: The two halves of the collar, black iron with the half name engraved: worth nothing, colder than ice and a dangerous thing to sell.
locations.secret: Under a rug at the edge of the circle lie Herluf’s last scratches, which Erland has covered so as not to see them: the whole name, scratched with a nail, and a small, crooked bell.

npcs.name: Erland Highfield
npcs.role: the villain, wizard and Ironmere’s healer
npcs.look: Tall, thin and dressed in grey, with thin leather gloves he never takes off and a grey toad on his shoulder that does not blink.
npcs.personality: Courteous, learned and ice-cold; proud as a man who has waited forty years to be proved right.
npcs.wants: To put Ukhraalesh in irons at midnight, gain the years it has eaten from the dead, and prove that Herluf was weak.
npcs.secret: Under the gloves his hands are black to the wrists, ever since he touched the circle the night Herluf vanished. He has never forgiven Yrsa for surviving, and he has kept her old iron amulet for forty years.
npcs.voice: Speaks low and slowly and uses the heroes’ names as if he had known them a long time. Straightens his gloves when he lies. “My master hesitated. I do not.”
npcs.where: The tower hall until 4 hours after sunset and then the crypt, where he waits by the circle

npcs.name: Yrsa
npcs.role: the old bell-ringer, once Master Herluf’s serving girl
npcs.look: Small and stooped in a grey cloak, with white hair, nails grey with salt and a white scar all the way around her neck.
npcs.personality: Quiet, stubborn and without fear; she believes she is dead, and the dead have nothing to lose.
npcs.wants: For the bell to ring again at midnight, and for no one else to lie in the circle as she did.
npcs.secret: She could have taken Herluf’s letter up to Erland forty years ago, but she kept it, because it was all she had left of Herluf. She loved him, and she wants to follow him through the door.
npcs.voice: Speaks of herself in the past tense and counts under her breath while she works. “I was a serving girl on Greytor. Now I only ring.”
npcs.where: Ironmere’s churchyard at sunset and the chapel ruin at midnight, as every night for forty years

npcs.name: Dyre
npcs.role: Erland’s apprentice, who wrote the letter without a sender, and the night’s gift
npcs.look: Seventeen, thin and pale, with ink on his fingers and an iron amulet around his neck that he must not take off.
npcs.personality: Helpful, nervous and eager to make something of himself; he admires his master and fears him just as much.
npcs.wants: To become a real wizard and get away from Greytor without betraying the only person who has ever looked after him.
npcs.secret: It was he who dug up Ironmere’s dead and carried them into the dovecote, and he has sold their jewellery to a fence in the city so that he can run away. He does not know that he himself is the gift.
npcs.voice: Talks too fast and apologises too much, calls Erland “master” and glances at the door whenever anyone mentions Greytor.
npcs.where: The Silent Birds in Ironmere; later with the heroes or in the cellar and, if nobody steps in, in the crypt

npcs.name: Einar Woodyard
npcs.role: elder of Ironmere and keeper of the inn
npcs.look: Broad and grey-bearded, with an apron over his Sunday clothes and a lead amulet on a cord that he keeps fingering.
npcs.personality: Proud, hospitable and stubborn; he defends whoever he owes thanks, even when he ought to know better.
npcs.wants: For his granddaughter to stay well, and for strangers to leave the valley’s healer in peace.
npcs.secret: He himself gave Erland leave to take the dead from the churchyard in return for medicine for the village, and his own wife, buried last winter, was among them.
npcs.voice: Speaks in short, firm sentences and raps his knuckles on the bar when he is done. “He saved my girl. I need know nothing more.”
npcs.where: The inn in Ironmere and the square in front of it, where the amulets can be burnt

npcs.name: Herluf
npcs.role: Erland’s master, vanished forty years ago
