npcs.look: Exists only as the letter H on the spines of books, a grey woollen cloak on a peg and a hasty, slanting hand.
npcs.personality: Learned and careful all his life and brave at the last; he chose to save a serving girl rather than finish his own work.
npcs.wants: For the door to stay shut, for the bell to ring every midnight, and for his apprentice to forgive him.
npcs.secret: He himself believed the bell would bind the demon, and he died because he understood too late that no name can.
npcs.voice: Speaks only through the letter and the bell. Read the letter aloud in a tired, kind voice that is in a hurry.
npcs.where: Herluf’s empty grave, the letter and the bell in the chapel ruin; he himself is behind the door in the crypt

npcs.name: Ukhraalesh
npcs.role: the demon behind the door, which Erland knows only as Ukhraal
npcs.look: A man-high, hunched carrion bird with a vulture’s bare grey neck and head, long arms with hooks for hands and wings like torn, tanned hide. It stinks like a slaughterhouse on a summer’s day.
npcs.personality: Hungry, patient and cheerful in a way that is worse than anger; it has waited forty years and can wait longer.
npcs.wants: To step through, eat the years the living have left, and first take the man who thought he could hold it.
npcs.secret: No name can bind it; the whole name and the bell can only drive it back. It fears the bell, and it was the demon that sent the little familiar to keep silent about the last syllable.
npcs.voice: Speaks only inside the heroes’ heads, with the voices of their own dead, and laughs whenever someone says the half name. “Call me again. I will come.”
npcs.where: The crypt, behind the door in the circle

rewards.name: Herluf’s Handbell
rewards.where: The tower hall, in the niche behind the fireplace’s iron fireback
rewards.description: A silver bell the size of an apple, cast from the same metal as the chapel bell, with the letter H on the handle. It can be rung once between one dawn and the next as a Magic action: every fiend within 30 feet that can hear it makes a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw and on a failure is Frightened until the end of its next turn.

rewards.name: Herluf’s Grey Cloak
rewards.where: The study, on the peg behind the door
rewards.description: A long grey woollen cloak with a black H sewn into the lining, which Erland never dared touch. It is a Cloak of Protection: while you are attuned to it, you gain a +1 bonus to AC and to saving throws.

rewards.name: Herluf’s Spellbook
rewards.where: The study, on the top shelves
rewards.description: Black leather, the letter H on the spine and a neat, slanting hand. It holds Magic Circle, Remove Curse, Dispel Magic, Counterspell, Glyph of Warding and Banishment, which a wizard can copy into their own book.

rewards.name: Erland’s Chest
rewards.where: The study, under the writing desk
rewards.description: An iron-bound chest with 260 gp in silver and gold, payment from the valley’s sick over twenty years.

rewards.name: Six Garnets
rewards.description: Six dark red garnets worth 50 gp each, wrapped in a handkerchief with Erland’s mark, a hand around a key.

rewards.name: Three Potions of Healing
rewards.where: The tower hall, in the cabinet by the patients’ benches
rewards.description: Three small clay jars of a bitter red draught, brewed by Erland for the village’s sick. Each restores 2d4 + 2 HP when drunk.

rewards.name: The Silver Bar
rewards.description: A small bar of silver that Erland uses to silver his finest amulets.

rewards.name: Dyre’s Purse
rewards.where: The dovecote, behind a loose stone by the east ladder
rewards.description: A worn leather purse with 34 gp from the sale of the jewellery of the dead and a scrap with the fence’s address. The money should go back to the bereaved.

rewards.name: The Jewellery of the Dead
rewards.description: Rings, brooches and clasps from Ironmere’s dead, among them a silver brooch shaped like a sheaf of corn. They belong to the families; if the heroes bring them back, they earn the village’s thanks instead of the money.

rewards.name: Ironmere’s Thanks
rewards.where: The inn in Ironmere, the morning after
rewards.description: Einar Woodyard, the elder, takes up a collection in the village and gives the heroes 120 gp in small coins and a promise of shelter in the valley for as long as they live. They get it only if the door is closed.

endings.success: The door closes in the crypt, and Ukhraalesh is gone. At dawn the birds lift from Ironmere’s roofs and fly away over the hills, and for the first time in seven days a blackbird sings. Dyre lives and will ring the bell every midnight from now on, as Yrsa did. The village burns the last amulets, buries its dead again and asks the heroes what should become of Greytor. If Erland went through the door, Yrsa carves a new name into Herluf’s stone.
endings.partial: The demon has been driven back or struck down, but at a cost: Dyre or Yrsa went through the door, or the sleepers of Ironmere saw what stood in the circle. The birds stay another month, silent, and Ironmere looks at the heroes with both gratitude and fear. If Erland lives, he has vanished with his familiar, and no one knows whether he will try again.
endings.failure: Ten rounds after midnight Ukhraalesh breaks up through the bell shaft and flies towards Ironmere. In the morning the birds are gone from the valley, and so is every soul who slept with an amulet around their neck; only those who were woken remain. The demon now hunts the valley, and it knows the heroes’ voices. The only way back leads through the bell, the whole name and a new circle, and someone must walk in through the door.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes kill or capture Erland before midnight.
unexpected.response: The door opens at midnight all the same, for it is the anchors that hold it open, not Erland. Without the collar there is not even an attempt at a binding: Ukhraalesh is free from the first round, and the familiar leads Dyre to the circle if he still wears the iron amulet.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes destroy the circle or sweep away the salt before midnight.
unexpected.response: The door still opens, but now nothing holds the demon in the crypt: the rule of the 10 rounds no longer applies, and it can break up through the bell shaft in the very first round. Herluf knew it; that is why the circle still stands.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes want to bind the demon themselves with the whole name.
unexpected.response: The whole name spoken into the collar holds it for one round (Restrained), and then it tears itself free and laughs. No chain holds it; Herluf’s letter says so, and it is true.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes reach the crypt only after midnight.
unexpected.response: Count the rounds from midnight: if the heroes arrive in round 6, they have 4 left. Erland lies bleeding by the circle or has fled, and Yrsa stands in the chapel striking the bell with her stone.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes want to take a long rest or wait for dawn.
unexpected.response: The night does not wait: at midnight the door opens, and 10 rounds later the demon is over Ironmere. Remind the players of the longcase clock in the hall and of the birds turning their heads before they decide.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes promise the familiar its freedom in return for telling them everything.
unexpected.response: It keeps the bargain and tells them the whole name and the truth about the circle, for it expects the heroes not to make it in time. Then it escapes, and it turns up again with a new master (see the sequel hooks).

tips: Keep the clock visible: put six dice on the table at sunset and take one away for every hour that passes. It is the night’s most important tool.
Make the birds a refrain: every time the heroes step outside, the birds are there, turning their heads. They never do anything until the door opens.

Write down the three anchors (the carrion, the call, the gift) and tick off each one the heroes break. Before the climax you will find the demon’s HP and abilities under the Door and the Three Anchors in the Crypt.
Print the written clues and put them in envelopes; Herluf’s letter should have a real wax seal for the players to break themselves.
Let Erland be right about everything except one syllable. It is his hubris that should frighten, not his power.
sequelHooks: The familiar got away with forty years of whispering. A scholar in the city has acquired a grey toad on his shoulder and has begun buying up old church bells.
Whoever keeps the two halves of the collar dreams of wings every night, and the demon now knows the heroes’ voices. It is waiting for someone to call it again, and someone will.
